Subject: Post-call: concurrency & multiplexing — pilot capacity / ratecard next steps

Hi Aisha — thanks for the call today. Quick recap and concrete asks so we can align the pilot: 

Summary (what we heard)
- FinPilot wants to run low-latency recommendation scoring + short streaming sessions for live personalization.
- Expected steady traffic: ~200–350 qps, peak burst up to ~550 concurrent inference requests.
- Average request size: 120 tokens in, 160 tokens out. Some streaming responses will be ~1–2kb over 30–45s.

Key requirements we flagged on the call
- P95 latency target: <= 800ms for standard generation paths; p50 ideally <150ms for short requests.
- Support for 400–600 parallel in-flight requests (connection multiplexing / parallel requests).
- Connection pooling across services (client side will multiplex; we need a matching server-side connpool and session occupancy profile).
- Streaming sessions: up to 45 minutes, keepalives, and graceful KV cache warmups for long-lived sessions.

Immediate asks / next steps
1) Can you confirm expected sustained concurrency vs. burst (numbers above) and whether 550 is a hard peak?
2) Please send procurement contact so we can prepare a pilot quote and any credit request.
3) We attached a simple "connection matrix" (finpilot_conn_matrix.xlsx) — fill in approximate qps per route and expected payload sizes.

Redwood proposal (pilot baseline) — high-level
- Reserved capacity (pilot): dedicated pool sized to support 500 concurrent requests with autoscale headroom for 700 bursts.
- Connection pool: server-side target of 300 persistent connections with multiplexing; client will maintain keepalive and multiplex up to X streams per connection.
- Token-rate guidance: we recommend planning for 120k tokens/min sustained with higher burst allowance for 2–5 minute windows.
- Streaming: we will enable streaming-optimized path with longer idle keepalive (60s) and periodic KV checkpointing.

I'll wait for your concurrency confirmation and procurement contact. If this looks good we'll slot the pilot for the week of Nov 29 (2-week pilot).

Thanks,
Priyom
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Thanks — Ben, Marissa. Technical follow-up with concrete config suggestions so SOW can include them verbatim: 

Suggested pilot configuration (technical)
- Pool type: Dedicated (single-tenant GPU pool) — avoids noisy neighbor variance for p95.
- Baseline pool sizing: equivalent of 4x high-memory inference GPUs (configured to sustain ~500 concurrent in-flight requests for the model family they described).
- Connection pooling / multiplexing: server-side connection pool target = 300 persistent connections; per-connection multiplexing up to 4 concurrent streams (gives ~1200 multiplexed concurrency headroom).
- Streaming settings: keepalive 60s, idle timeout 10m for long sessions; implement KV-cache warmup on session reopen to reduce p95 on resumed sessions.
- Token limits & throttles: pilot token-rate soft cap = 150k tokens/min with configurable burst windows; hard caps only if client exceeds agreed safety thresholds.
- Fallback policy: route to a smaller quantized model variant if latency > 1.5s or capacity constrained; we will test failover in pilot.

Observability + success criteria (add these to SOW)
- p50/p95 latency per route (goal p95 <= 800ms).
- Successful sustained concurrency test at 500 concurrent for 30 minutes without >5% error rate.
- Streaming session stability: <1% disconnects over 24h simulated run.

Action items / timeline
1) Aisha: confirm final peak concurrency (you said 550 — is that peak for US-East only?).
2) Aisha: confirm procurement contact (you provided accounts-payable@finpilot.com — we'll send quote).
3) Ben/Marissa: I'll drop the technical sizing above into the pilot SOW draft and attach redwood_slo_draft.pdf.
4) Aisha: requested start week Nov 29 — please confirm preferred start date.

I'll prepare a smoke-test plan we can run the week prior for warmup and KV seed.

—Priyom
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
